From ef3b04091fd8bc737dc45312375df8625b8318e2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alok Tiwari <alok.a.tiwari@oracle.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 00:28:31 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm/a6xx: move preempt_prepare_postamble after error
 check

Move the call to preempt_prepare_postamble() after verifying that
preempt_postamble_ptr is valid. If preempt_postamble_ptr is NULL,
dereferencing it in preempt_prepare_postamble() would lead to a crash.

This change avoids calling the preparation function when the
postamble allocation has failed, preventing potential NULL pointer
dereference and ensuring proper error handling.

Fixes: 50117cad0c50 ("drm/msm/a6xx: Use posamble to reset counters on preemption")
Signed-off-by: Alok Tiwari <alok.a.tiwari@oracle.com>
Patchwork: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/687659/
Message-ID: <20251113082839.3821867-1-alok.a.tiwari@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robin.clark@oss.qualcomm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_preempt.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_preempt.c
index afc5f4aa3b17..747a22afad9f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_preempt.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_preempt.c
@@ -454,11 +454,11 @@ void a6xx_preempt_init(struct msm_gpu *gpu)
 			gpu->vm, &a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_bo,
 			&a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_iova);
 
-	preempt_prepare_postamble(a6xx_gpu);
-
 	if (IS_ERR(a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr))
 		goto fail;
 
+	preempt_prepare_postamble(a6xx_gpu);
+
 	timer_setup(&a6xx_gpu->preempt_timer, a6xx_preempt_timer, 0);
 
 	return;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

### Modifications in each file

- **`drivers/gpu/drm/msm/adreno/a6xx_preempt.c`**:  
  The call to `preempt_prepare_postamble(a6xx_gpu)` was moved from before the `if (IS_ERR(a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr))` error check to after it.

### Relationships between the modifications

The reordering ensures that `preempt_prepare_postamble()` is only invoked after confirming that `preempt_postamble_ptr` is valid (not an error pointer). Previously, if the allocation of the preemption postamble buffer failed, `preempt_prepare_postamble()` would attempt to dereference the invalid pointer, causing a NULL pointer dereference and a crash. By moving the call after the error check, the function now properly skips preparation when the allocation fails, aligning with the intended error-handling flow.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr = msm_gem_kernel_new(gpu->dev, ...);</text>
<text>preempt_prepare_postamble(a6xx_gpu);</text>
<text>if (IS_ERR(a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr)) // check after call</text>
Reason:
The function `preempt_prepare_postamble()` dereferences `a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr` internally, but it is called before the `IS_ERR()` check. If `msm_gem_kernel_new()` returns an error pointer (e.g., on allocation failure), the subsequent call to `preempt_prepare_postamble()` will dereference this invalid pointer, leading to a NULL pointer dereference and a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (IS_ERR(a6xx_gpu->preempt_postamble_ptr))</text>
<text>    goto fail;</text>
<text>preempt_prepare_postamble(a6xx_gpu);</text>
Reason:
By moving the `IS_ERR()` check before the call to `preempt_prepare_postamble()`, we ensure that the function is only invoked when `preempt_postamble_ptr` is a valid pointer. If the check fails, we jump to the error handling path (`fail`), which disables preemption and cleans up, thus preventing any dereference of an invalid pointer.
